# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan: 4 Days for 2 Adults

A comfortable Kyoto route for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** that keeps transfers short, uses **one hotel only**, and includes **temples, gardens, local food, and one half-day shopping stop**.
Budget target of **$1,800 total excluding international flights** is very workable with a mid-range hotel, transit, meals, and admissions.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival + Classic Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive and check in near Kyoto Station or Gion for easy transit and shorter walks.
- **Afternoon:** Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, and Ninenzaka; keep the pace slow and use rest stops in the neighborhood.
- **Dinner:** Kyoto-style tofu or yudofu set near Gion; easy first-night meal with minimal walking.
- **Local transport:** **JPY 1,200–2,000** for 2 adults
- **Walk load:** Moderate, but can be kept under 20 minutes between stops if you use a taxi for the uphill segment to Kiyomizu-dera.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens + Riverside Temple Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, and the temple garden.
- **Afternoon:** Okochi Sanso Garden or a riverside tea break; keep this as your scenic, slower-paced day.
- **Dinner:** Tempura or soba in Arashiyama, then return to hotel early.
- **Local transport:** **JPY 1,400–2,400** for 2 adults
- **Walk load:** Light to moderate; good option for using the Randen line and short taxi hops.

### Day 3: Low-Energy Temple + Food Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Start with **Nijo Castle** or **Nanzen-ji** depending on energy; both work well with shorter walking segments.
- **Afternoon:** Slow lunch and a relaxed temple/garden combo such as Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or Shosei-en Garden.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/64/Gate%2C_Sh%C5%8Dsei-en%2C_Kyoto_-_Apr_3%2C_2013.jpg Alt=Afternoon:** Slow lunch and a relaxed temple/garden combo such as Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or Shosei-en Garden, Kyoto, Japan
- **Dinner:** Nishiki Market area for small plates, yuba, pickles, sweets, and sake tasting.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Dinner:** Nishiki Market area for small plates, yuba, pickles, sweets, and sake tasting, Kyoto, Japan
- **Local transport:** **JPY 1,000–1,800** for 2 adults
- **Walk load:** Low; this is the best day to protect the knee and use taxis for any long transfer.

### Day 4: Half-Day Shopping + Final Kyoto Sights
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Half-day shopping in **Kyoto Station / Porta / Kyoto Yodobashi** or **Shijo-Kawaramachi** for souvenirs, snacks, and local goods.
- **Afternoon:** Short final temple stop such as Kennin-ji or a return to a favorite area for photos and coffee.
- **Dinner:** Farewell kaiseki-lite, ramen, or izakaya near your hotel.
- **Local transport:** **JPY 1,000–1,800** for 2 adults
- **Walk load:** Light; shopping can be done mostly indoors with easy breaks.

## Ranked Stay Plan and Budget Fit

| Item | Recommended Choice | Why it fits | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hotel | 1 mid-range hotel near Kyoto Station or Gion | Single base, easy transit, less walking | **$650–$950 total** |
| Food | Mix of casual set meals, market snacks, and 1 nicer dinner | Matches food interest without overspending | **$320–$520 total** |
| Local transport | Subway, buses, and a few short taxis | Best for knee comfort and short hops | **$60–$110 total** |
| Admissions | Temples, gardens, castle, small entry fees | Plenty of variety with modest entry costs | **$50–$120 total** |
| Shopping | Souvenirs and local goods | Keeps the trip flexible | **$80–$180 total** |
| Buffer | Taxis, drinks, extra snacks | Useful for comfort and weather changes | **$100–$150 total** |

**Estimated total for 2 adults:** **$1,260–$2,030**
A realistic target is **about $1,500–$1,750** if you keep the hotel mid-range and use taxis selectively for the knee-friendly days.

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in Mid-April

- **Comfortable walking shoes** with good cushioning
- **Light jacket or cardigan** for cool mornings and evenings
- **Compact umbrella** or rain shell
- **Knee support or brace** if it helps on temple stairs
- **Small day bag** for water, snacks, and tickets
- **Portable phone charger**
- **Cash card mix**: some yen cash plus a credit card
- **Socks easy to remove** for temple visits
- **Reusable water bottle**
- **Basic pain relief items** approved for personal use
- **Light layers** for changing spring temperatures
- **Shopping tote** for souvenirs and market purchases
